item.description: DigitalCommons@UTEP (The University of Texas at El Paso) — As data increasingly shapes participation in society, there is growing emphasis on preparing youth to engage with data through computer science education. item.description: Springer eBooks — This chapter examines the complex relationship between migration, urban food access, and the COVID-19 pandemic. South Africa’s urban areas are popular destinations for migrants seeking economic opportunities, education and healthcare, as well as relative stability. While many respondents reported improvements in food security following migration, the study reveals that they still face persistent barriers to food security due to intersecting factors such as economic constraints, limited mobility, and a local food environment that lacks adequate access to culturally appropriate foods. item.description: Springer eBooks — This chapter investigates the heightened food insecurity experienced by Zimbabwean, Somali, and Congolese migrants in Cape Town, South Africa, during and post the COVID-19 pandemic. item.description: Springer eBooks — The COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa manifested as a syndemic, in which the virus interacted with pre-existing comorbidities and inequalities in food security, employment, and social protection to intensify vulnerability. Migrants and refugees were among those most severely affected, both because of their concentration in precarious forms of work and because they were systematically excluded from government relief measures. item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Indonesia’s customs administration operates at the intersection of maritime mobility, trade facilitation, border protection, and revenue assurance, yet its risk systems are still primarily organized around declarations, manifests, entities, and transactions rather than the wider maritime operating picture. This article develops a conceptual model for transforming Maritime Domain Awareness into a Customs Risk Picture that can support earlier, more contextual, and more explainable targeting of vessels, voyages, cargoes, and commercial actors. item.title: Staying under climate change: review of drivers, outcomes and intersectional dimensions of immobility
item.description: Frontiers in Climate — Climate change is increasingly framed as a driver of human migration, yet migration is not a universal response to climate stress. Many individuals and households remain in place despite climatic, economic, and social risks, raising important questions about why people stay, under what conditions, and with what consequences. This paper undertakes an exploratory review of the literature on human immobility in the context of climate change. item.description: Discover Sustainability — Abstract Globally, marine pollution generated by oil spills, plastic litter, and industrial waste poses major threats to the environment, the economy, and human health. Field surveys, optical sensing, and manual sampling are examples of traditional monitoring and mitigation techniques that are frequently hampered by inefficiency, poor precision, and restricted coverage, particularly in large-scale or remote circumstances. item.title: Socio-economic flood resilience reveals welfare-vulnerable communities obscured by asset-based appraisals
item.description: Research Square — Abstract Asset-based flood risk assessments can obscure inequalities in welfare impacts. We integrate two-metre-resolution flood hazard maps, socioeconomic data and a dynamic recovery model to quantify socio-economic flood resilience (SEFR), defined as asset loss divided by monetised well-being loss. Analysis of 6,791 English neighbourhoods across flood sources and return periods under present-day and future RCP8.5 conditions reveals highly unequal household asset and well-being losses. item.title: A Theoretical Study on the Conceptual Integration of Plasticity and Resilience in Lifespan Developmental Psychology
item.description: Journal of Education Humanities and Social Sciences — Over decades, lifespan developmental psychology has gradually developed a research paradigm centered on the entire life course. Within this framework, "plasticity" and "resilience" have emerged as two key concepts, each reflecting human development from different perspectives—plasticity emphasizing changeability and adaptability, while resilience highlighting stability and stress resistance. item.description: Springer eBooks — This chapter examines how the COVID-19 pandemic reshaped food insecurity, health, and gendered responsibilities among Somali migrants and refugees in Kitchener-Waterloo. Using photovoice, participants documented the everyday effects of rising food prices, disrupted income, and the loss of communal food practices that had long functioned as informal safety nets. item.description: Scientific Reports — Abstract The interaction between pilots and Air Traffic Controllers (ATC) is essential for aviation safety. Operational demands, time pressure, and differences in perceived workload may contribute to communication difficulties and conflict during pilot–controller interactions. This study examines the relationships among communication and teamwork, conflict management, perceived workload, perceived performance, and previous relevant training exposure. item.description: Radical Housing Journal — At the fringes of São Paulo’s macro-metropolis, precarious housing often meets fragile environments. In these peripheral neighbourhoods, grassroots groups have been reinventing the housing-environment nexus and remaking the peripheries on their own terms. This paper conceptualises these struggles as housing-environment activisms. item.title: A description of the health-related built environment surrounding Ontario social housing sites
item.description: Frontiers in Built Environment — Introduction The built environment is a key determinant of health, particularly for older adults living in social housing who often experience high rates of chronic disease. This study aimed to assess the health-related built environment surrounding social housing sites across Ontario, focusing on the availability and accessibility of healthcare facilities, pharmacies, grocery stores, public transit, and recreational spaces. item.description: Singapore Journal of Tropical Geography — This paper addresses lacunae in critically thinking about temporal entanglements between digitalization and urbanization in global peripheries. item.description: Radical Housing Journal — Cities of the Global South are at the forefront of the climate and environmental crisis, where climate change acts as a threat multiplier on existing social, economic, political and spatial inequalities. This paper asks how to frame and address the climate crisis amidst long-standing housing inequalities in the Global South, through the case of housing for waste workers adjacent to the Bhalswa landfill in Delhi, India. item.title: Craniofacial Growth Transformer: A Growth-Aware Framework for Longitudinal Craniofacial Analysis and Forecasting
item.description: Research Square — Abstract Accurate characterization of craniofacial growth is important for orthodontic planning, craniofacial assessment, and long-term monitoring of facial development. Most existing methods rely on sparse or cross-sectional data. As a result, they do not fully capture how facial structures change over time or how different facial regions develop together.This study presents a growth-aware framework for longitudinal craniofacial analysis and forecasting. The framework is based on a dense longitudinal dataset containing nearly ten years of near-daily facial observations from three individuals.

item.description: Springer eBooks — The introductory chapter outlines the context and rationale for the book. It examines how the COVID-19 pandemic led to profound food security and socioeconomic challenges for migrants and refugees while exacerbating longstanding structural inequalities. These groups were often disproportionately affected by the pandemic and excluded from, or marginalised within, relief measures. item.description: CAUCHY Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi — Binary regional classification of food security is often complicated by class imbalance and spatially heterogeneous predictoroutcome relationships. This study applies Firth Penalized Class-Weighted Geographically Weighted Logistic Regression (Firth CW-GWLR), which combines geographically weighted estimation, class weighting, and Firth's penalty on each local likelihood to reduce small-sample bias and protect against separation. item.description: Microbiology — Urbanization is rapidly increasing worldwide, with increasing attention focused on its consequences for human populations. Despite the importance of outdoor urban environments for biodiversity and human wellbeing, their microbial ecology remains poorly characterized, particularly in relation to emerging microbial threats including antimicrobial resistance (AMR). item.description: Discover Cities — The process of urbanization is accompanied by alterations in the urban climate behavior, and this in turn is characterized by spatial-temporal variations in temperature that are related to the urban and environmental characteristics of the city. In this context, urban morphology and vegetation are a strategy for reducing the impact of microclimate during periods of high temperature. item.title: Hidden and fragmented patterns of morphological informality across African cities revealed by open geospatial data
item.description: Computers Environment and Urban Systems — Abstract Informal settlements are among the fastest-growing forms of urbanization, yet their spatial distributions within cities remain under-represented and inconsistently documented in official statistics and global urban datasets. Conventional assessments often identify large, contiguous informal neighborhoods but miss smaller and fragmented forms embedded within otherwise formal urban areas. item.title: Visualizing Maritime Governance Research: What Scopus Data Tells Us, with Insights into Indonesian Researches
item.description: Journal of Maritime Policy Science. — Maritime governance crosses legal, security, environmental, and economic domains, but the connections among its scholarly conversations remain unevenly understood. This article provides a bounded bibliometric map of 196 English-language journal articles retrieved from Scopus on 15 October 2026 using the exact phrase “maritime governance” in titles, abstracts, or keywords (2001–2026). item.title: Digital rural transformation, financial assets, and rural household wellbeing
item.description: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems — Existing research treats rural digitalization mainly as a transaction-cost shock and pays little attention to a second margin: by improving access to financial services, markets and investment opportunities, digital rural transformation may enable rural households to accumulate financial assets and thereby improve their economic well-being. Using pooled panel data from the 2015, 2017 and 2019 waves of the China Household Finance Survey (CHFS), we empirically analyze the impact of digital rural transformation on rural households' consumption structure and the mediating role of financial assets.

item.description: Journal of Environmental Studies and Sciences — Abstract Plastic waste is commonly addressed through technological, regulatory, and behavioral approaches, yet the role of collective artistic practice in shaping relationships with discarded materials remains underexplored. item.title: Impact Investing in Agribusiness: Financial Returns, Food Security and Sustainability Trade-offs
item.description: Asian Journal of Agricultural Extension Economics & Sociology — Impact investing has become an influential proposition for financing agribusinesses expected to generate both commercial returns and measurable social or environmental benefits. Yet investment intent, enterprise growth and development impact remain analytically distinct. This critical narrative review examines whether and under what conditions agribusiness impact investment can reconcile financial viability with food security, nutrition, ecological sustainability and distributive justice. item.description: Forest Ecology and Management — Primary European beech ( Fagus sylvatica ) forests represent fundamental sources of information regarding natural stand dynamic processes, disturbance regime, as well as abiotic and biotic stressors that shape the structure, functioning and biodiversity of conspecific forest ecosystems across the continent. item.description: Research Square — Abstract This study shifts the reading of open space from separate spatial categories toward a heterogeneous everyday open-space system, because characteristics that support use in one space type may not work similarly in another. In dense informal settlements, neighbourhood streets, house yards, residual land, fields, inundated vacant spaces, and river edges are collectively used for everyday activities. item.description: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change — Introduction Ecological boundaries separate habitats, whereas disciplinary boundaries can separate ways of understanding them. Whether empirical ecological patterns can provide a basis for structural analogy across disciplinary boundaries remains poorly understood. item.description: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change — Objective This study audits the comparability of municipal forest-cover and reported governance-activity records in a compilation centered on 2024 for Zhejiang, China. item.description: Frontiers in Neurology — Background The vertebrobasilar system is the primary blood supply to the posterior circulation, and basilar artery tortuosity is a common morphological variation. Previous studies have suggested that basilar artery curvature may increase the risk of posterior circulation infarction (PCI). This study evaluated the association between basilar artery displacement distance and posterior circulation infarct phenotype among patients with acute ischemic stroke. item.title: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and Fraud Prosecution in Oyo State
item.description: Research Square — Abstract Fraud continues to be a pervasive challenge in Nigeria, undermining governance, destabilizing institutions, and eroding public trust. This study investigates the prosecution of fraud by the Anti-Fraud Unit of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Oyo State, focusing on patterns, perpetrators, tactics, and systemic constraints. item.description: Springer eBooks — This chapter examines Ecuador’s response to COVID-19 by analysing pandemic-era policies in social protection, migration, and food systems within broader governance shifts already underway: the humanitarian turn in migration governance and the convergence of austerity and authoritarianism in responses to social crisis. item.title: Digital transformation and public health emergency management capacity: epidemic pressure as a constraint and innovation capacity as an enabler
item.description: Frontiers in Public Health — Background Digital transformation is increasingly embedded in public health systems, but its contribution to emergency management may depend on the conditions under which digital resources are deployed. Existing research has focused primarily on specific digital technologies, leaving limited evidence on whether broader digital transformation is associated with stronger public health emergency management capacity at the regional level and how this relationship varies across epidemiological and innovation environments. item.title: Leadership and organizational sustainability among NGOs working with displaced populations in Greece
item.description: Journal of International Humanitarian Action — Abstract Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) play a central role in ensuring protection, emergency aid and basic services for displaced populations. Guided by the Job Demands–Resources model, this study aims to generate knowledge about how NGO leaders in Greece interpret job demands affecting fieldworkers and organizational functioning, and how resources are mobilized to mitigate these demands and thereby support sustained humanitarian work. item.description: Accident Analysis & Prevention — Wildfires create rapidly changing conditions for roadway operations and safety, yet how wildfire-related conditions relate to crash occurrence and injury severity remains insufficiently understood. Using data from 10 California wildfires between 2020 and 2025, this study examines crash occurrence at the roadway segment-day level and injury severity at the crash level through two separate machine-learning analyses. item.description: Scientific Reports — Ambient air pollution is a recognized risk factor for influenza-like illness (ILI). However, it remains unclear how city-specific characteristics modify these associations. This study evaluated the short-term associations between six major air pollutants and ILI incidence in Shandong Province, China, and investigated the modifying effects of seasonal, spatial, and socioeconomic factors. item.description: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management — Abstract Sustainable urban logistics requires innovative solutions that reconcile operational efficiency and economic viability while complying with sustainable mobility requirements. This study investigates the role of multidimensional flexibility in enabling sustainable last-mile urban logistics, with a specific focus on electric cargo bikes used in last-mile urban logistics. item.description: Environmental Policy and Governance — ABSTRACT In federated systems of government, state governments have become pivotal in steering climate change adaptation through a range of instruments. item.description: Sustainable Development — ABSTRACT Enhancing tourism resilience (TR) is vital for absorbing shocks, ensuring sustainability, and boosting regional competitiveness; yet systematic evaluation and tailored improvement strategies remain urgent challenges. item.title: Fruit fly control with the Sterile Insect Technique: male-only versus bisexual releases-Modeling, analysis, and simulations
item.description: Journal of Mathematical Biology — The Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) is a target-specific and environmentally friendly method for controlling invasive agricultural pests such as tephritid fruit flies. Although male-only releases represent the current gold standard, the high costs and technical complexity of sex-sorting technologies make bisexual releases a practical necessity in some regions.
